column2: Both Moses and Aaron receive the divine speech; the following plural command matches the two addressees.
The permitted animals are selected from earthly animals. May eat expresses legal permission in the future form.
Divided hoof, two hoof divisions and bringing up cud are cumulative criteria. The anatomical wording remains provisional.
column3: How best to express the repeated hoof/claw vocabulary without confusing English readers?

column2: The camel begins the exceptions: cud-bringing is affirmed and divided hoof denied. The ancient description is not scientifically rewritten.
Dasypous is provisionally hare; the source order places it before choirogryllios. The physiological statement remains as given.
The inherited transliteration choirogryllios avoids an unverified zoological identification but leaves a lexical decision open.
column3: Which supported English animal label best renders choirogryllios in this Greek context?

column2: The pig meets the hoof criterion but not the cud criterion. Both positive details and the negative remain.
Eating flesh and touching carcasses are separately prohibited. Carcasses retains the death qualification rather than forbidding all living contact.
Both fins and scales are required; waters, seas and streams remain explicit, without restricting the rule to marine fish.
The disallowed aquatic creatures include what waters bring forth and every living creature therein. No narrower species class is inserted.
The two responses differ: do not eat flesh and abhor carcasses. The repeated abomination designation is retained.
The rule restates fins and scales together; the inherited wording is read as absence of the required combination.
column3: Would lacks fins or scales express the legal condition more clearly without flattening the conjunction?

column2: Eagle and sea-eagle flank gryps. Gryps remains untranslated pending lexical decision; it must not be automatically identified as a modern vulture species.
column3: Should gryps be rendered griffin, or does contextual evidence support a bird designation?

column2: Vulture differs from the preceding gryps. Those like it follows kite; the scope is not redistributed over every listed bird.
Raven and things like it form their own entry. The similarity expression is retained rather than replaced with modern taxonomy.
Ostrich, owl, gull and hawk remain in order, with likeness clauses after gull and hawk. Exact bird identities remain provisional.
Night-raven, diving bird and ibis are separate terms. Diving bird keeps katarraktes broad rather than certifying a modern species.
Purple waterbird, pelican and swan preserve three entries. The descriptive first rendering does not certify a species-level identification.
Owl occurs again in the Greek, followed by heron, plover and its likeness group, hoopoe and bat. The repeated owl is not deleted.
The category is winged creeping things walking on four. The ancient classification remains, without importing modern insect leg counts.
The exception describes legs above feet used for leaping. The functional description is retained without anatomical reconstruction.
Four named kinds each have a likeness clause. Brouchos and attakes remain lexical debts; snake-fighter is a descriptive rendering, not a certified identification.
column3: Resolve these insect names from specialist Greek evidence; no successful full lexical consultation is credited here.

column2: The four-footed winged-creature prohibition resumes after the exception. No only is added to the number of feet.
Contact with carcasses causes uncleanness until evening. The duration belongs to the person touching them.
Carrying adds garment washing to the until-evening condition. It is not collapsed into the preceding touching rule.
This Greek wording positively describes divided hoof and claws but negates cud chewing. No missing negative is supplied from another textual base.
Propose paws for hands in the quadruped context. LSJ cheir I.3 explicitly covers animal paws and cites this passage; the close stage preserves the inherited literal hands wording.
Carrying carcasses requires washing garments and waiting until evening; the final general uncleanness statement remains.
Weasel, mouse and land crocodile preserve the Greek list. Land crocodile is literal and provisional, not a claim of modern zoological identification.
Five additional animal labels remain distinct. Spotted lizard and the other inherited identifications require specialist confirmation.
column3: Confirm the zoological range of mygale, kalabotes and aspalax without harmonizing the Hebrew list.

column2: The contact rule explicitly applies when these creatures are dead. The English does not extend it indiscriminately to living animals.
Wood, cloth, skin and sack articles are dipped, remain unclean until evening, then become clean. Washing does not erase the time interval.
An earthenware vessel receives different treatment: contents become unclean and the vessel itself is broken.
Food exposed to water and drink in a vessel are separately mentioned. The inherited wording leaves the contextual contamination linkage unexpanded.
column3: How should the water clause be explained within the preceding vessel condition?

column2: Ovens and pot-stands are demolished, with repeated uncleanness language. The distinct cooking installations are not flattened into vessels.
Springs, cistern and collected water form an exception; touching carcasses still defiles the person. The contrasting subjects remain.
Sowing seed remains clean when a carcass falls on it. Dry is not inserted, though the next verse contrasts poured water.
Water poured upon seed changes the ruling when carcass contact follows. Both conditions remain explicit.
Even an otherwise edible animal creates carcass-contact uncleanness if it dies. The permitted food class is retained.
Eating and carrying have separate prescriptions; the Greek expressly adds bodily bathing for the carrier. This clause is not omitted by harmonization.
The ground-creeping category receives the abomination label and eating prohibition. The passive shall not be eaten is preserved.
Belly movement, four-footed movement and many feet remain. Continually represents dia pantos provisionally; its construction needs further review.
column3: Does dia pantos qualify walking continually, or introduce the full many-footed category?

column2: The emphatic first negative and two further defilement negatives remain. Souls renders the personal object without adding a separate spiritual doctrine.
Divine holiness grounds commanded sanctification and holiness. The repeated Lord your God and renewed prohibition are present in this Greek source.
The exodus is expressed as bringing up from Egypt in order to be their God. The repeated holiness requirement remains.
The summary covers animals, birds, aquatic life and ground-creeping life. It is not reduced to livestock alone.
Clean/unclean and edible/inedible contrasts are retained. Living creatures is provisional: the participle zoogonounton may convey breeding or producing life and requires closer lexical work.
column3: Does the Greek describe live-bearing creatures or a broader living category, and how should the following neuter article be construed?

column2: The Lord addresses Moses alone here, unlike the joint address opening chapters 11 and 13.
Receiving seed and bearing a male precede seven days of uncleanness compared with menstrual separation. No moral judgment is added to the ritual terminology.
The eighth day governs circumcision. The Greek verb is third-person singular with no explicit agent; inherited he is retained provisionally.
column3: Would an English passive clarify the unnamed circumciser without obscuring the active Greek construction?

column2: Thirty-three days and unclean blood reflect the Greek reading. Touching holy things and entering the sanctuary remain distinct restrictions.
A female birth entails twice seven days and sixty-six days. The repeated unclean blood wording is not normalized to a different textual base.
The completed period applies to either son or daughter. An unblemished year-old lamb and either young pigeon or turtledove have separate offering roles.
The priest presents, makes atonement and cleanses her from the blood-source. Fountain retains the source metaphor; the concluding law includes both sexes.
The means idiom allows two birds in place of the lamb. One bird is for the whole offering and one for sin; cleansing follows priestly atonement.
Moses and Aaron jointly receive these instructions. The introductory formula does not name a modern medical authority.
The bright scar-like mark and lesion terminology remain provisional. Leprosy represents lepra without certifying a modern disease; the person is brought to Aaron or a priestly son.
column3: Review lesion terminology as an ancient ritual classification, including oule and semasia, rather than assume a modern diagnosis.

column2: White hair and a depressed appearance together support the priest's ruling. Declare unclean renders the causative verb's ritual function here.
A white bright spot without depression or white hair is isolated seven days. The faint qualification and lesion as grammatical object remain.
On the seventh day an unchanged lesion leads to a second seven-day separation. The Greek switches its object from lesion to person.
Faintness without shifting permits a clean ruling, followed by garment washing. Neither the priestly decision nor the washing is omitted.
Change and shifting after examination for cleansing require another appearance. The two motion expressions are retained provisionally without diagnosing spread beyond the wording.
The priest sees the shifted mark and declares uncleanness. The final leprosy designation remains explicit.
A lesion arising in a person initiates coming to the priest. No fixed waiting period is added to this introduction.
White scar, white hair and sound living flesh occur together. The difficult partitive flesh phrase is represented cautiously as some.
column3: How best to convey sound living flesh in this ritual diagnostic contrast?

column2: The Greek directs isolation after declaring longstanding leprosy. The positive isolation command is not changed to the negative found in some familiar English forms.
Abundant outbreak and total coverage from head to foot are bounded by the priest's complete visual examination.
All-white coverage receives a clean ruling, however unexpected to modern readers. As to the lesion represents the second accusative provisionally.
column3: Confirm the relationship of auton and ten haphen in the clean declaration.

column2: Appearance of living skin changes the status on that day. The passive defiled does not insert a moral act.
The sound skin is grammatically the agent making him unclean. The translation preserves this unusual clause rather than substituting the priest as subject.
Restoration and whitening lead to another priestly visit. The inherited restored remains provisional for the return/change sequence.
The priest declares the lesion clean, then the man is clean. The shifts of reference remain explicit.
An ulcer in the skin that heals introduces a separate conditional case. The verse intentionally continues into the next.
White scar and whitish or red bright spot are alternative appearances at the former ulcer site. The colour alternatives are not collapsed.
Depressed appearance and whitening hair lead to uncleanness; the outbreak is explicitly located in the ulcer.
No white hair, no depression and faintness lead to seven-day separation. All three diagnostic negatives/qualifications remain.
Spreading triggers the ruling, and the source repeats that leprosy blossomed in the ulcer. The repeated clause is retained.
Remaining in place without spreading is treated as an ulcer scar. The priestly declaration differs from the preceding outcome.
The case concerns a fire burn and its healed area. White with reddish colouring and complete whiteness remain distinct alternatives.
Hair whitening and depressed appearance identify an outbreak in the burn. Both leprosy statements remain rather than being merged.
Absent white hair, no depression and faintness again require seven days. The shining spot remains the local referent.
The emphatic spreading expression supports indeed. The Greek says ulcer at the end even within the burn case; it is not harmonized to burn.
Stable, unspread and faint appearance is a burn scar. Scar and mark remain distinct descriptions in the clean ruling.
The rule includes man or woman and head or beard. No attempt is made to rewrite the ancient category into a modern clinical formulation.
Hollow appearance and fine yellowish hair lead to uncleanness. Broken patch is a provisional rendering of thrausma, with head and beard leprosy distinguished.
column3: Which natural English term best preserves thrausma without importing a modern disease identification?

column2: No hollow appearance and no yellowish hair lead to isolation. Yellowish, rather than black, is the selected Greek wording here.
The seventh-day inspection checks no spread, no yellowish hair and no hollow appearance. The three-part condition continues into shaving instructions.
Skin is shaved, but the patch itself is not. A second seven-day separation follows; the two shaving clauses must remain opposite.
After shaving, stable non-hollow appearance permits a clean ruling and washed garments. The second inspection retains the same day count.
Emphatic spreading after cleansing reopens the case. The sentence continues into the priestly examination next verse.
Once spread is observed, checking yellow hair is no longer required. The negative inspection command is retained without treating it as negligence.
Remaining in place and new black hair signify healing. He is clean precedes the priest's clean declaration, preserving both statements.
Man or woman with shining whitish patches begins another case. The whiteness terms are descriptive, not a new disease label.
White eruption is provisional for alphos. The text twice says he is clean, and both declarations remain.
column3: Confirm alphos and the repeated shining/whitish vocabulary through specialist lexical review.

column2: Loss of head hair by itself is baldness and clean. No uncleanness is inferred from hair loss alone.
Front-of-head hair loss is separately designated and also clean. The English keeps the location distinction.
White or fiery-red lesion on either bald area changes the category. The disjunction is not silently converted to a blended colour.
The examined appearance is white with redness and resembles skin leprosy. The colour description here differs in construction from verse 42.
The doubled defilement expression supports surely declare unclean. The head location closes the diagnostic ruling.
Loose garments, uncovered head, mouth covering and being called unclean follow the Greek. Neither torn garments nor shouting Unclean is substituted automatically.
Uncleanness lasts while the lesion remains. Dwelling apart and residence outside camp are both specified.
The same lepra vocabulary now applies to wool or coarse-flax garments. Its broad ancient use is not equated with modern human leprosy.
Warp, weft, linen, wool, leather and worked leather remain in sequence. The source list is not shortened to fabrics and skins.
Greenish or fiery-red appearance in the listed materials prompts showing it to the priest. The shower's identity remains implicit.
The priest examines and isolates the lesion for seven days. The repeated priest subject is source-supported.
Spread in fabric or worked leather yields persistent leprosy. Persistent reflects emmonos without inventing a biological mechanism.
The affected article is burned with fire because the condition persists. Both the instruction and restated passive burning remain.
Absence of spread in the listed articles introduces the washing alternative. No clean ruling is prematurely inserted.
The priest commands, someone washes, and the priest isolates again. The intermediate singular agent is implicit; inherited he remains open.
column3: Is the washer the priest or an unnamed person acting on his instruction?

column2: Unchanged appearance can require burning even without spread. Both negative conditions are retained, preventing a false rule that no spread always means clean.
Faintness after washing leads to tearing out the affected part. The source distinguishes removing a part from burning the whole item.
Reappearance is a renewed outbreak requiring burning of the affected article. Again is supported by eti here.
Departure of the lesion after washing is followed by a second wash and a clean status. The extra wash is explicit.
The summary covers wool, coarse flax, warp, weft and leather, with both possible rulings. Declare clean/unclean retains the adjudicative purpose.
